subject: Day 78: first parent-baby swim
bodyText:
Today's focus
First day in the pool. Treat it as a sensory and social outing, not a skills lesson; warm water, slow movements, and your face close are the entire curriculum.

Action items
- Attend the first parent-baby swim class and keep it short and calm; at 3 months the goal is comfort in water with you, and AAP notes infant classes do not water-proof a baby, so supervision rules never relax. AAP HealthyChildren, swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Keep the rest of the day light around the outing, since a new environment plus an extra wake window can run him toward overtired; bank any lost sleep with an earlier bedtime rather than a late nap.
- Continue 400 IU/day of vitamin D if he is exclusively or predominantly breastfed; pool or sun time does not replace the supplement. AAP HealthyChildren, vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Pack a labeled bag for the class with a swim diaper, towel, a feed for after, and a warm layer, and plan to feed soon after since the water and activity will burn energy.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Mild post-swim fatigue and a bigger appetite afterward; both are expected after a new, active outing.
- [monitor] Shivering or persistent fussiness in the water, which usually means the pool is too cool for him; keep sessions brief and the water warm.
- [call within 24h] New cough, congestion, or eye redness in the day after the class; note onset and call if it persists or worsens.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, choking, blue lips, or labored breathing after a water swallow is a same-day call, and 911 immediately for blue lips or breathing trouble!

Enrichment opportunities
- Hold him chest-to-chest through the water introduction so your reassuring face stays in view; secure, smooth movement is the whole lesson at this stage. AAP HealthyChildren, swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Support him in arm-supported floats and gentle reaches in the water; the buoyant resistance is novel motor input that complements floor tummy time. AAP HealthyChildren, movement birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Narrate the water in a calm running commentary (splash, kick, float, warm) and pause for his sounds; the live language plus serve-and-return is the active ingredient for later language. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep consolidation window opens (~3 months); start the consistent sleep-wake routine
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2
- Weeks 14-18: 4-month sleep regression onset for many infants

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
